findings.title: Update invalidation uses organization-decorated state instead of the stored IDP state
findings.body: `idpById` is obtained through `getById`, which wraps organization-bound providers and makes `isEnabled()` depend on the organization being enabled. The new login-cache invalidation predicate therefore sees an IDP in a disabled organization as not login-capable even when its stored `enabled` flag is true. For example, after a public IDP has been cached while its organization is disabled, changing it to `hideOnLogin=true`, `linkOnly=true`, or non-public makes both the decorated original and the updated model fail the predicate, so `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` does not clear the list cache. The cache-hit path reloads the IDP by ID but never reapplies the hide/link/public filters, so it can return the removed provider; once the organization is enabled again it can be displayed on the login page despite the update. Determine membership changes from the raw persisted original model (or invalidate for these field changes regardless of dynamic organization enablement).

findings.title: The new test registers cleanup for a nonexistent identity-provider alias
findings.body: The cleanup callbacks at lines 381 and 425 are bound to `identityProviders().get("alias")`, but this test only creates `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-20`. Teardown therefore attempts to remove an unrelated/nonexistent provider and leaves the newly created providers in the test realm, which can leak state into later tests or cause duplicate-alias failures on reruns. Register cleanup using each generated alias instead.
